label: D1 update gate: high after reaching S1 (esp. via a2 rare), low after S2 via a1
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * (prev_state == S1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * (prev_state == S2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_state == S1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_state == S2) ;; (phase == D1) * choice
explanation: Raw update gate z of unit 0. It saturates near 1 at GO and D2, and the variation that matters is at D1 (mean ~0.49, falling late in the episode). Beyond timing, the D1 value depends on the previous trial choice x reached state, and the reward hardly matters (fitted weight ~-0.01). Relative to the first-trial baseline: a2->S1 (rare) is about +0.29, a1->S1 (common) +0.19, a2->S2 (common) -0.14, a1->S2 (rare) -0.28. So the gate is mostly high after S1 and low after S2, and the rare transitions push it further each way. The model policy logit at D1 (choice, a model output) has a negative weight, so a stronger lean toward a1 means lower z. That term adds about 0.09 R^2 within the cells. Test R^2 beyond timing: 0.70 with the four observed choice x state terms alone (plus a reward term, which adds nothing), and 0.79 with the D1 policy term added; the profile ceiling all = 0.84 and all observed = 0.75. Rewards, the trial before last, the hidden good state and time since reversal add little (<0.01).

issues: The quoted weights (+0.29 a2->S1, +0.18 a1->S1, -0.15 a2->S2, -0.28 a1->S2) depend on the D1 policy-logit term, which is collinear with the cells. Without that term the four cells fit +0.08 (a1S1), -0.42 (a1S2), +0.40 (a2S1), -0.09 (a2S2), test R^2 0.70. So on the observed-only fit the common transitions sit close to baseline and nearly all of the swing comes from rare transitions. Additively that is about +0.49 for S1 plus about +0.32 for a2. 'Mostly high after S1 / low after S2' still holds, but the size of the common-cell effects depends on the model.
Reward is not completely irrelevant. After S2 its weight is about -0.05 (misses: D1 after a1 S2 r is over-predicted by -0.088). It adds only about 0.004 test R^2, so 'hardly matters' stands.

The worst-fit windows are mostly the window's first D1, where the previous trial is unknown (prev_action = -1). There the actual z is about 0.03-0.05 against about 0.4 predicted. Observed terms in the window can't fix this, and it is a minor error class.

Checked and confirmed: test R^2 is 0.789 with the choice term and 0.70 without it, so the term adds 0.09. Episode-decile x state interactions, the trial before last, a stay/repeat term and value each add <0.005. The gate saturates near 1 at GO and D2, and the baseline residuals there are below 0.007.
